correctness.rationale: The prime-power criterion \(\sigma(p^j)\mid\sigma(p^a)\iff j+1\mid a+1\) follows from gcd of powers minus one. Full-complement divisors are distinct witnesses yielding the exact lower bound (1). A single defect forces exactly one exponent 2 or 3. In these cases the only potentially bad exponent is a-1, and cancellation gives \(\sigma(p^{a-1})\mid\sigma(m/e)\). The single-prime omitted-cofactor tests are both necessary and sufficient. Edge cases n=1 and m=1 and the unique bad divisor are established. Infinitude and zero density follow from standard prime progression theorems and a square-divisibility tail; finite checks do not replace proof.

value.rationale: The natural defect of multiplicative divisor-sum compatibility over the divisor lattice has a complete first-positive fiber with a canonical unique violating divisor, infinite congruence families, and zero-density rarity. The sharp general blockwise obstruction explains why all other exponent patterns require at least two failures. This is not a routine finite table calculation.
